tldr: Wealthsimple dominated the day with a sweeping launch: an AI assistant (Penny), instant client-to-client transfers, commission-free CAD options and a Pro trading platform. Elsewhere, BMO is rolling out agentic AI in its contact centre, Chime is expanding its product set, and Latin American players had crypto and Pix outages plus a new yield feature from Nequi.
themes: AI assistants and agents in banking apps
Wealthsimple's push into trading and payments
Service outages and third-party dependency risk

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple launches Penny, an AI assistant that prepares e-transfers, pays invoices, flags duplicate card charges and helps self-directed investors trade. It always asks for client confirmation and has ChatGPT and Claude connections.
highlights.why: The most direct competitor has shipped an action-taking AI assistant in banking and trading, which raises the bar for what Canadian digital-bank customers expect from in-app AI.

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple makes CAD options commission-free, cuts a mobile trade from 8 steps and 21 seconds to 2 steps and 4 seconds, and will launch Wealthsimple Pro with Level 2 data in late November.
highlights.why: This puts pricing and speed pressure on Simplii's self-directed trading offer and sets a new benchmark for mobile trade flow.

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple Pay allows instant transfers of up to $100,000 between Wealthsimple clients, alongside temporary virtual cards with custom expiry dates and spending limits.
highlights.why: High-limit instant transfers and controllable virtual cards are new payment and security features that Simplii customers may start to ask for.

highlights.headline: BMO rolls out AI Agent Assist in its Virtual Connect contact centre for credit card queries (transaction matching, policy retrieval, case prep), targeting up to 30% shorter call times. Chime also reports its Jade AI agent in Q3 results.
highlights.why: Big Canadian banks are putting agentic AI into servicing, so Simplii should weigh the same efficiency gains and faster resolution for its own contact centre.
